about: Adelaide-based space technology company operating nanosatellite constellations for IoT connectivity and developing ground-penetrating mineral exploration technology (ExoSphere). ExoSphere combines seismic sensors in the field with satellite links and AI to image underground deposits, sold as a service to miners. Founded in 2018 by Flavia Tata Nardini. Customers include mining firms and governments. Funding shown is about $170 million. B2B brand, known in Australian space and mining circles.
cb_desc: Fleet Space Technologies is an Al-powered SpaceTech...

about: San Diego-based treasury and finance software company, offering cloud-based cash and liquidity management, payments and risk tools to large corporates. Founded in 2000 by Jean-Luc Robert, it connects to thousands of banks and sells subscriptions to corporate treasury, finance and risk teams around the world. Venture and growth investor-backed with about $167 million. B2B software brand, widely used by large corporate treasurers.

Seattle-based industrial analytics software company whose Seeq platform lets engineers analyze time-series data from plants for process manufacturers. Its Workbench and Organizer tools sit on top of historians and cloud data lakes, sold by subscription and through Microsoft Azure and AWS marketplaces. Customers include oil, pharmaceuticals and energy companies. Founded in 2013. Funding shown is about $165 million. B2B software brand.
cb_desc: Seeq is a software company that accelerates industrial...

about: Dedham, Massachusetts-based AI-powered cloud platform for investment accounting and fund administration, used by insurers, asset managers and banks. Venture-funded with about $156 million. B2B fintech brand.
cb_desc: FundGuard is an artificial intelligence-powered and clou...

about: Teleste is a Turku, Finland-based technology group, listed on Nasdaq Helsinki (TLT1V), offering broadband cable access equipment, video security and information systems for rail and public transport. Customers include cable operators and railway networks. Revenue is around 150 million euros. B2B with little consumer awareness.

wiki.title: Teleste
wiki.text: Teleste Oyj is an international technology group in broadband, security and information technologies and related services. The company's customer base consists of data communications operators, train manufacturers, public transport operators, and public sector organizations.

about: MakinaRocks is a Seoul-based South Korean industrial AI start-up, offering Runway MLOps and anomaly detection software for manufacturing and data analysis. Customers are major Korean manufacturers. Raised about $40 million. B2B software with little public awareness. Crunchbase shows total funding of $40,190,553 and a headquarters in Seoul, South Korea; check the input data for scale.

Pindrop is an Atlanta, Georgia company providing voice authentication and fraud detection software that analyses calls to contact centres, so banks, insurers and retailers can spot fraud and deepfakes. Founded in 2011, it has raised about $300 million in total, including a large debt financing in 2024. Privately held with B2B customers; little public awareness.

MuleSoft is a San Francisco integration and API software company, whose Anypoint Platform connects applications, data and devices for enterprises. Founded in 2006, it was listed on the NYSE in 2017 and acquired by Salesforce in 2018 for about $6.5 billion, and now operates as a Salesforce business. Customers are large enterprises. B2B with little consumer awareness; Salesforce is well known in sports sponsorship.

wiki.title: MuleSoft
wiki.text: MuleSoft, LLC. is an American software company headquartered in San Francisco that provides a unified platform for integration, API management, and managing multi-agent systems.

about: Auros is an on-demand human insight platform, based in Bellevue, Washington, apparently connecting companies to consumer research and feedback. Its products, customers and scale are not described further in the input. A small B2B technology business. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)
cb_desc: Auros is an on-demand human insight platform designed to...

wiki.title: Auros
wiki.text: Auros is a commune in the Gironde department in southwestern France.

about: BMC Software is a Houston enterprise software company for IT operations and service management, known for mainframe tools, BMC Helix and Control-M, serving large enterprises, governments and banks. It has been privately owned by KKR since 2018 and split into two companies in 2025. B2B with little public awareness.

wiki.title: BMC Software
wiki.text: BMC Software, Inc. is an American multinational information technology (IT) services and consulting, and enterprise software company. In 2025, the company's Helix product was spun off into the independent IT service and operations-focused company, BMC Helix.

about: Domo is an American Fork, Utah business intelligence and data platform company, whose cloud product connects data sources and builds dashboards for business users. According to the input, it is now part of Progress Software. Domo was founded in 2010 by Josh James and listed on Nasdaq (DOMO). B2B software brand with limited consumer awareness.
cb_desc: Domo is now part of Progress Software. The Progress Domo...

wiki.title: Domo, Inc.
wiki.text: Domo, Inc. is an American cloud software company based in American Fork, Utah, United States. It specializes in artificial intelligence, business intelligence, and data visualization and is designed to provide real-time access to business data for decision makers across the company with minimal IT involvement. It is a software as a service venture.

about: Getronics is an information and communications technology services group, with a UK office in Reading, which provides cloud, workplace, networking and managed services to enterprises. The brand has a long history in the Netherlands and has changed owners several times. Its current scale and structure are not confirmed here. B2B with low consumer awareness. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)
cb_desc: The Getronics family is an ICT Services group consisting of...

wiki.title: Getronics
wiki.text: Getronics is a Dutch-headquartered ICT services business, founded in 1887 and today employing approximately 4,000 employees across Europe, Asia Pacific, and Latin America. Getronics is also founding member of the Global Workspace Alliance, a consortium of leading local IT companies delivering IT services in over 180 countries.

about: Transmit Security is a Tel Aviv identity and security company, offering a customer identity and access management (CIAM) platform with passwordless authentication, fraud prevention and identity verification for banks and large enterprises. Founded in 2014 by Mickey Boodaei and Rakesh Loonkar, it raised a record $543 million Series A in 2021, at a valuation of $2.2 billion. B2B with limited consumer awareness.

wiki.title: Transmit Security
wiki.text: Transmit Security is a private cybersecurity and identity and access management company based in Tel Aviv, Israel and Boston, Massachusetts. Founded by Mickey Boodaei and Rakesh Loonkar in 2014, Transmit Security provides companies with customer authentication, identity orchestration, and workforce identity management services. In June 2021, the company completed a Series A funding round by raising $543 million, which was reported to be the largest Series A in cybersecurity history. Transmit Security is a FIDO Alliance Board member.

about: Druva is a Santa Clara, California cloud data protection company offering a SaaS platform for backup, disaster recovery, ransomware protection and data resilience across endpoints, servers, SaaS apps and cloud workloads, built on AWS. Customers are enterprises worldwide that pay subscriptions. Founded in 2008 in Pune, India, it has raised around 475 million dollars, with a valuation of about 2 billion dollars in 2021, and serves more than 6,000 customers. It is private and has limited public brand awareness outside IT circles.

wiki.title: Druva
wiki.text: Druva Inc. is an American privately held software company. The company provides SaaS-based data protection and management products.

about: Own Company, formerly OwnBackup, is a data protection and management platform headquartered in Englewood Cliffs, New Jersey. Its software backs up, restores and secures SaaS data, mainly Salesforce, with archiving and seeding tools, serving thousands of enterprise customers. It was founded in 2015 and acquired by Salesforce in 2024 for about 1.9 billion dollars, and has raised around 507 million dollars as an independent. B2B subscription revenue. Brand awareness is limited outside Salesforce administrators.

Aiven is a Helsinki, Finland cloud data infrastructure company offering managed open source data services such as PostgreSQL, MySQL, Apache Kafka, ClickHouse, OpenSearch and Redis-compatible tools across AWS, Google Cloud, Azure and others. Customers are developers and enterprises paying usage-based fees. Founded in 2016, it has raised about 420 million dollars, with a 2022 round at a 2 billion dollar valuation. It is private. B2B, mainly known among developers and engineers, little consumer awareness.

Cellebrite is an Israeli-American digital intelligence firm, with US presence in Vienna, Virginia and main offices in Petah Tikva, Israel. It sells mobile forensics and data extraction tools such as UFED, plus cloud analytics, to police, intelligence, defense and corporate investigators in over 100 countries. Revenue is around 400 million dollars. Founded in 1999, it listed on Nasdaq (CLBT) in 2021 via a SPAC merger, with Sun Corporation as a major holder. B2B and government, with limited consumer awareness.

wiki.title: Cellebrite
wiki.text: Cellebrite DI Ltd. is an Israeli digital forensics company headquartered in Petah Tikva that provides tools for law enforcement agencies as well as enterprise companies and service providers to collect, review, analyze and manage digital data. Their flagship product series is the Cellebrite UFED.

about: Eightfold AI is a Santa Clara, California software company whose AI-based Talent Intelligence Platform helps employers hire, retain and develop staff, using skills matching for recruiting, internal mobility and workforce planning. Customers are large enterprises paying subscriptions, including companies in tech, finance and retail. Founded in 2016 by Ashutosh Garg and Varun Kacholia, it raised about 400 million dollars, with a valuation of 2.1 billion dollars after its 2021 round led by SoftBank. B2B, limited consumer awareness.

wiki.title: Alexandra Levit
wiki.text: Alexandra Levit is an American writer, consultant, speaker, workplace expert, and futurist. She has written ten business and workplace books and writes as a syndicated columnist for the Wall Street Journal.

about: JumpCloud is a Louisville, Colorado cloud directory platform that lets IT teams manage user identities, devices (Windows, Mac, Linux, mobile), single sign-on, multi-factor authentication and access to apps and networks from one console. Customers are small and mid-size businesses and managed service providers worldwide, paying per-user subscriptions. Founded in 2012 by Rajat Bhargava, it has raised about 417 million dollars, with a valuation around 2.6 billion dollars in 2022. It is private. B2B, known among IT administrators, with little consumer awareness.

wiki.title: JumpCloud
wiki.text: JumpCloud is an American enterprise software company headquartered in Louisville, Colorado. The company was formally launched in 2013 at TechCrunch Disrupt Battlefield with its announcement of an automated server management tool. JumpCloud offers a cloud-based directory platform that centralizes identity, access, and device management for both human and non-human identities.

about: Signifyd is a San Jose, California e-commerce fraud protection company. Its platform decides in real time whether online orders are legitimate and guarantees against chargebacks, also handling returns abuse and account takeover. Customers are retailers and brands such as Peloton and Lacoste, who pay per-order fees. Founded in 2011, it raised about 409 million dollars, with a 1.3 billion dollar valuation in 2021. It is private. B2B, with little consumer awareness.

wiki.title: Signifyd
wiki.text: Signifyd is an American technology company that develops fraud protection and abuse prevention technology. It is based in San Jose, California.

about: Aviatrix is a Santa Clara, California cloud network security company whose platform provides secure connectivity, visibility and policy enforcement across AWS, Azure, Google Cloud and Oracle Cloud. Customers are large enterprises and government bodies that pay subscriptions. Founded in 2014, it has raised about 340 million dollars from investors including Sequoia, Tiger Global and CIT. It is private. B2B, known mainly to cloud and network engineers, with no consumer awareness.

wiki.title: Aircraft pilot
wiki.what: Person controlling an aircraft in flight
wiki.text: An aircraft pilot is an individual who controls an aircraft's flight by operating its directional controls. Other aircrew members, such as navigators and flight engineers, are also considered aviators because they assist in operating the aircraft’s navigation and engine systems. Aircrew members like drone operators, flight attendants, mechanics, and ground crew are not classified as aviators.

about: DataStax is a Santa Clara, California database software company built around Apache Cassandra, offering the Astra DB cloud database and tools for building generative AI applications with vector search, plus Langflow. Customers are enterprises such as Verizon, Home Depot and Capital One. Founded in 2010, it raised about 343 million dollars and was acquired by IBM in 2025. B2B, known among developers and data engineers, with no consumer awareness.

wiki.title: DataStax
wiki.text: DataStax, Inc. is a real-time data for AI company based in Santa Clara, California. Its product Astra DB is a cloud database-as-a-service based on Apache Cassandra. DataStax also offers DataStax Enterprise (DSE), an on-premises database built on Apache Cassandra, and Astra Streaming, a messaging and event streaming cloud service based on Apache Pulsar. As of June 2022, the company has roughly 800 customers distributed in over 50 countries.

about: Drata is a San Francisco compliance automation company whose trust management platform automates evidence collection and continuous monitoring for frameworks such as SOC 2, ISO 27001, HIPAA and GDPR. Customers are technology companies and growing businesses, which pay subscriptions. Founded in 2020, it raised about 328 million dollars, with a 2 billion dollar valuation in 2022. It is private. B2B, with strong awareness among security and compliance teams and little consumer visibility.

Ironclad is a San Francisco contract lifecycle management software company. Its AI-powered platform handles contract creation, workflow, negotiation, approval and storage for legal, sales and procurement teams, used by customers such as L'Oreal, Mastercard and OpenAI. Founded in 2014, it raised about 334 million dollars, with a 3.2 billion dollar valuation in 2022. It is private. B2B, known to in-house lawyers, with little consumer awareness.

wiki.title: Ironclad warship
wiki.what: Steam-propelled warship protected by armor plates
wiki.text: An ironclad was a steam-propelled warship protected by steel or iron armor constructed from 1859 to the early 1890s. The ironclad was developed as a result of the vulnerability of wooden warships to explosive and incendiary shells. The first ironclad battleship, Gloire, was launched by the French Navy in November 1859, narrowly preempting the British Royal Navy. However, Britain built the first completely iron-hulled warships.

about: Loadsmart is a Chicago freight technology company with an AI-driven platform that matches shippers with carriers for truckload, intermodal and drayage freight, and offers a transportation management system. Customers are enterprise shippers, brokers and carriers, earning from freight margins and software fees. Founded in 2014, it raised about 346 million dollars, with backers including Maersk and Tiger Global. Private. B2B logistics brand with little consumer awareness.

At-Bay is a San Francisco insurtech that provides cyber insurance and technology errors and omissions coverage for businesses, using security scanning data and risk tools to underwrite and help clients improve defenses. Customers are small to mid-size businesses sold via brokers. Founded in 2016, it raised about 296 million dollars with a 1.35 billion dollar valuation in 2021. Private. B2B insurance brand with limited consumer awareness.

BigPanda is a Redwood City, California software company with an AIOps platform that correlates alerts across IT monitoring tools and automates incident response for large IT operations teams. Customers include enterprises and telecoms like Intel and Cisco, paying subscriptions. Founded in 2012 in Israel and the US, it raised about 313 million dollars, with a 1.2 billion dollar valuation in 2021 led by Insight Partners. Private. B2B, well known only to IT operations teams.

wiki.title: BigPanda
wiki.what: Software company headquartered in Redwood City, California
wiki.text: BigPanda is a private software company headquartered in Redwood City, California. BigPanda Incident Intelligence and Automation, powered by AIOps, supports companies to prevent service outages and improve incident management.

about: Matillion is a Salford, UK data integration software company, founded in Manchester in 2011, whose cloud-native platform loads and transforms data into warehouses such as Snowflake, Databricks, Amazon Redshift and Google BigQuery. Customers are enterprises worldwide paying subscriptions. It also has a major presence in Denver. It raised about 290 million dollars, valued around 1.5 billion dollars in 2021. Private. B2B, known among data engineers, with little consumer awareness.

Versa Networks is a Santa Clara, California networking and security company offering SASE, SD-WAN and secure access service edge software, which converges WAN connectivity and cloud security for enterprises and service providers. Customers include large corporations, telecoms and managed service providers, paying subscriptions. Founded in 2012, it raised about 316 million dollars and is valued above 1 billion dollars. Private. B2B, with no consumer awareness.

Salt Security is a Palo Alto, California API security company, with an Israeli R&D base. Its platform uses AI to discover APIs, detect attacks and block threats for enterprises. Customers are large companies in finance, retail and technology. Founded in 2016, it raised about 271 million dollars, with a valuation of 1.4 billion dollars in 2022. Private. B2B, with no consumer awareness.

Scandit is a Zurich, Switzerland smart data capture company that provides barcode scanning, text recognition and augmented reality software that turns smartphones, tablets and wearables into scanners. Used by retailers, logistics, healthcare and manufacturing firms, with customers including large grocery and parcel companies, paid by licenses. Founded in 2009 as a spin-off from ETH Zurich, it raised about 273 million dollars. Private. B2B, with no consumer awareness.

wiki.title: Scandit
wiki.text: Scandit AG, commonly referred to as Scandit, is a Swiss technology company that provides smart data capture software. Their technology allows any smart device equipped with a camera to scan barcodes, IDs and text and to perform additional functions using augmented reality and advanced analytics.

subsector: Analytics, Data Integratio... San Diego, California
about: Tealium is a San Diego, California customer data platform company offering tag management, data orchestration, identity resolution and AI-based predictions that help marketers collect and activate customer data across channels. Customers are large brands in retail, financial services, travel and media paying subscriptions. Founded in 2008, it raised about 264 million dollars, with a valuation around 1.2 billion dollars after 2021 funding. Private. B2B, with no consumer awareness.

wiki.title: Tealium
wiki.text: Tealium is an American company founded in 2008 in San Diego, California, that sells enterprise tag management, an API hub, a customer data platform with machine learning, and data management products. It has offices in the United States, Singapore, UK, Germany, Japan, Netherlands, France and Australia.

about: Tools for Humanity is a San Francisco and Berlin technology company, cofounded by Sam Altman and Alex Blania, that builds Worldcoin's World Network, including the Orb iris scanner, World ID and the Worldcoin token. It aims to verify human identity online and distribute crypto. It raised about 244 million dollars, including a 2023 round led by a16z and Bain Capital Crypto. Private. Well known in tech and crypto circles with mixed regulatory attention.

wiki.title: Tools For Humanity
wiki.text: Tools for Humanity is a private technology company based in San Francisco and Munich. Since 2019, it has been a major contributor to World, and it also makes the Orb, a hardware device that is built to verify humanity and create a unique “digital credential” for users. Tools for Humanity has raised approximately US$200 million from investors such as Blockchain Capital, Bain Capital and Andreessen Horowitz.

about: New Relic is a San Francisco observability software company founded in 2008 that provides tools to monitor application performance, infrastructure and digital experience for engineering teams. Customers are enterprises in many sectors, with revenue near 1 billion dollars. It listed on the NYSE (NEWR) in 2014 and was taken private in 2023 by Francisco Partners and TPG in a deal valuing it at about 6.5 billion dollars. B2B, known by developers, with no consumer awareness.

wiki.title: New Relic
wiki.what: American web tracking and analytics company
wiki.text: New Relic, Inc. is an American web tracking and analytics company based in San Francisco. The company's cloud-based software allows websites and mobile apps to track user interactions and service operators' software and hardware performance.

about: Exiger is a McLean, Virginia risk and compliance technology company that provides AI-driven supply chain risk, third-party risk and financial crime compliance software and services. Customers are governments, defense agencies, banks and large corporates. Founded in 2012, it has raised about 182 million dollars and has Canadian and UK operations. It is private. B2B, known in compliance circles, with no consumer awareness.
cb_desc: Exiger provides technology- enabled risk and compliance...

about: Jobber is an Edmonton, Alberta cloud software company that helps home service businesses such as lawn care, cleaning and plumbing firms with scheduling, quoting, invoicing and payments. It serves over 200,000 service professionals in North America and elsewhere. Founded in 2011, it raised about 183 million dollars. Private. B2B, with moderate awareness among small trades businesses and little consumer awareness.

Together AI is a San Francisco AI cloud company that lets developers run, fine-tune and train open-source AI models on GPU clusters through an API. Customers are AI startups and enterprises paying for compute and inference. Founded in 2022, it has raised over 500 million dollars, including a 2025 round at a multi-billion dollar valuation. A B2B developer brand. Customers are paying users of its GPUs and models, and it is among the fast-growing AI infrastructure startups. Its brand is known to developers, not consumers.

Securiti is a San Jose-based data security and privacy software company founded in 2019. Its Data Command Center platform uses AI to discover sensitive data across clouds and SaaS apps, and automates governance, privacy compliance, access controls and AI-security. Customers are large enterprises and regulated organisations, paying subscription fees. It raised about 156 million dollars from investors including Mayfield and General Catalyst, and was acquired by Veeam in a roughly 1.7 billion dollar deal announced in 2025. B2B software with little public brand awareness.

Allot is an Israeli communications software company based in Hod Hasharon that provides network intelligence, security and monetisation solutions. Its products include Allot NetworkSecure, DNS and endpoint security services for mobile and broadband operators, plus traffic management and analytics. Customers are telecom operators and enterprises worldwide, who pay through software, subscription and service fees. It is listed on Nasdaq (ALLT) and founded in 1996. B2B technology brand with little consumer awareness.

wiki.title: Allot Ltd.
wiki.text: Allot Ltd., formerly Allot Communications, is an Israeli high-tech company that develops telecommunications software. The company is headquartered in Hod Hasharon, Israel.

about: Grid Dynamics is a digital engineering and software services firm headquartered in San Ramon, California, with large delivery teams in Eastern Europe, Poland, India and other locations. It builds cloud, data, AI and e-commerce platforms for retailers, consumer goods makers, finance, technology and healthcare clients, working on a time-and-materials or project basis, with revenue of roughly 350 million dollars. It is listed on Nasdaq (GDYN). B2B services firm with little consumer awareness.

Ebix is a US software and services company, previously based in Johns Creek, Georgia, serving insurance, financial and travel customers with insurance exchange software, claims, payments and remittances (including EbixCash in India), and e-learning. Revenue was around 1 billion dollars before it filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in December 2023 and sold its businesses to Eraaya Lifespaces. It was listed on Nasdaq (EBIX) until delisted. B2B brand with little public awareness.

wiki.title: Ebix
wiki.text: Ebix, Inc., previously known as ebix.com, Inc. and formerly Delphi Information Systems, Inc., is an American multinational technology company which focuses on e-commerce, cloud computing (SaaS), insurance, finance, healthcare and e-learning. Co-founded by Ken Bitticks in Atlanta, Georgia in 1976, it was traded on Nasdaq as EBIX. The company's global headquarters is located in Johns Creek, Georgia, with offices in Australia, Brazil, Canada, India, New Zealand, Singapore and UK.

about: Nota AI is a South Korean AI optimisation company in Seoul, spun out of KAIST, whose NetsPresso platform compresses and optimises deep learning models so they run on small edge devices. It also sells intelligent transportation and vision solutions, and works with Samsung, Qualcomm and Nvidia-related partners. Revenue comes from software licences and solutions. It raised about 41 million dollars and listed on the Korean KOSDAQ in 2025. B2B AI technology, no consumer profile.

Trust Stamp (Trust Stamp, now T Stamp Inc.) is an Atlanta-based AI identity software company offering facial biometric authentication, liveness checks, privacy-preserving identity tokens and fraud-prevention tools, which serve banks, fintechs, governments and enterprises worldwide, with offices in Malta, the UK, Rwanda and the Philippines. Revenue is licensing and service fees. It is listed on Nasdaq (IDAI). B2B technology brand with little consumer awareness.

Macnica Galaxy is a Taiwanese AI technology subsidiary of Japan's Macnica Holdings, based in Taipei, working on AI hardware and software solutions and distribution for edge devices, industrial customers and technology firms. It has raised around 761 million new Taiwan dollars. It is listed on Taiwan's stock market. B2B technology brand with no consumer awareness. Specific products are not confirmed here. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Gnosis is a blockchain infrastructure company, registered in Gibraltar, building decentralised tools on Ethereum including Gnosis Chain, Safe (formerly Gnosis Safe) multi-signature wallets, CoW Protocol, and Zodiac. It started in 2015 with prediction markets and raised money through a 2017 token sale, with funding recorded at about 212 million dollars. The GNO token governs the ecosystem. Crypto-sector brand with no consumer awareness beyond blockchain users.

wiki.title: Gnosis
wiki.text: Gnosis is the common Greek noun for knowledge. The term was used among various Hellenistic religions and philosophies in the Greco-Roman world. It is best known for its implication within Gnosticism, where it signifies a spiritual knowledge or insight into humanity's real nature as divine, leading to the deliverance of the divine spark within humanity from the constraints of earthly existence.

about: Unizen is a Liechtenstein-based digital asset trading platform, based in Vaduz, that aggregates liquidity from decentralised and centralised exchanges and offers a unified swap and trading interface, together with its UZN token. Customers are crypto traders and institutions, and revenue is from trading fees. Recorded funding is about 200 million dollars, which seems large for the company. Crypto-sector brand with little awareness outside the crypto community. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)
cb_desc: Unizen is a digital asset exchange platform that..

wiki.title: Presidio
wiki.text: A presidio was a fortified base established by the Spanish Empire mainly between the 16th and 18th centuries in areas under their control or influence. The term is derived from the Latin word praesidium meaning protection or defense.

about: Open-source blockchain network for smart contracts and digital assets, launched in 2018 after a 2017 token sale that raised over $230 million, founded by Arthur and Kathleen Breitman. The Tezos Foundation in Zug, Switzerland, supports development and grants. Used by NFT marketplaces, brands and financial applications with its XTZ token. Funding of about $242 million shown. Known in crypto circles and has used sports and media sponsorships, but not a mainstream consumer brand.

wiki.title: Tezos
wiki.text: Tezos is an open-source blockchain that can execute peer-to-peer transactions and serve as a platform for deploying smart contracts. The native cryptocurrency for the Tezos blockchain is the tez. The Tezos network achieves consensus using proof-of-stake. Tezos uses an on-chain governance model that enables the protocol to be amended when upgrade proposals receive a favorable vote from the community. Its testnet was launched in June 2018, and its mainnet went live in September 2018.

about: Clavister is a Swedish cybersecurity company based in Ornskoldsvik, founded in 1997, that builds network security software and firewalls under the cOS Core and cOS Stream names. It sells to telecom operators, managed security service providers, governments and enterprises, and since 2020s increasingly to defence and military vehicle makers through its onWire and Defence Grade products, with Swedish and European customers. It is listed on Nasdaq Stockholm under CLAV. Crunchbase shows about $39 million in funding. B2B brand with low consumer awareness.

wiki.title: Clavister
wiki.text: Clavister is a Swedish company specialized in network security software, listed on NASDAQ First North.

about: GLG (Gerson Lehrman Group) is a US expert network, based in New York and founded in 1998 by Mark Gerson and Thomas Gerson, connecting investors, consultants and corporations with experts through calls, surveys and events. Its research platform serves hedge funds, private equity and large corporations, with offices in North America, Europe and Asia. It is privately owned and raised about $412 million as shown by Crunchbase in 2015. B2B brand, widely known in financial research circles.

Verafin is a Canadian financial crime management software company, based in St. John's, Newfoundland, whose cloud platform detects fraud and money laundering for banks and credit unions in North America. Founded in 1990, it had more than 3,000 institutional customers. Nasdaq acquired Verafin in 2020 for $2.75 billion and it is now part of Nasdaq's financial technology business. B2B brand, no consumer awareness.

wiki.title: Verafin
wiki.text: Verafin Inc. is a Canadian fraud detection technology and anti–money laundering software company based in St. John's, Newfoundland and Labrador, Canada. The company was established in 2003 by Jamie King, Brendan Brothers, and Raymond Pretty.

about: LaunchDarkly is a US software company, based in Oakland, California, whose feature management platform lets engineering teams release, toggle and test software features safely, with experimentation and AI model configuration tools. Customers are thousands of software companies and enterprises, paying subscription fees. Founded in 2014, it raised about $330 million and was valued near $3 billion in 2021. Privately held. B2B developer brand, with no consumer awareness.

Qumulo is a US enterprise file storage software company, based in Seattle, founded in 2012, whose scale-out file data platform runs on-premises and in public clouds for media, healthcare, research and government customers. It sells subscriptions and raised about $347 million. Privately held. B2B software brand with no consumer awareness.

wiki.title: Qumulo
wiki.text: Qumulo is an American data storage company based in Seattle, Washington. Founded in 2012, it offers products and services to help other companies manage and curate large amounts of data.

about: Redis is a US data technology company, based in Mountain View, California, which commercialises the open-source Redis in-memory database, used for caching, real-time data and AI applications, through Redis Cloud and Redis Enterprise. Customers are developers and enterprises, including large internet companies. It has raised about $357 million, valued at $2 billion in 2021, and has changed its licence several times. B2B developer brand, widely known among software engineers.

wiki.title: Redis
wiki.text: Redis is an in-memory key–value database, used as a distributed cache and message broker, with optional durability. Because it holds all data in memory and because of its design, Redis offers low-latency reads and writes, making it particularly suitable for use cases that require a cache.

wiki.title: Redis (company)
wiki.text: Redis Ltd. is an American private computer software company headquartered in San Francisco, California. Redis is the sponsor of the source-available in-memory NoSQL database Redis, and the provider of Redis Enterprise software, cloud services, and tools for global companies. The company’s research and development center is based in Tel Aviv, Israel. It has additional offices in London, Austin, Bengaluru, and Sofia.

about: SnapLogic is a US enterprise software company, based in San Mateo, California, founded in 2006 by Gaurav Dhillon, whose integration platform as a service (iPaaS) connects applications, data and APIs with a low-code interface and AI agents. Customers are large enterprises, paying subscription fees. It raised about $371 million, including a $165 million round in 2021. Privately held. B2B software, with no consumer awareness.

wiki.title: SnapLogic
wiki.text: SnapLogic is a commercial software company that provides an integration platform as a service (iPaaS) for connecting cloud computing data sources, SaaS applications, on-premises business software and APIs. Founded in 2006 by Gaurav Dhillon, former CEO and co-founder of Informatica, the company is headquartered in San Mateo, California. SnapLogic is now led by Brad Stewart and is venture-backed by firms including Andreessen Horowitz, Ignition Partners, Microsoft, Silver Lake Waterman, Sixth Street and Capital One Ventures.

about: Unqork is a US no-code enterprise application platform, based in New York, founded in 2017 by Gary Hoberman. It lets banks, insurers and governments build complex software with visual tools rather than hand-written code. Customers include large financial firms and public agencies, paying subscriptions. It raised about $365 million, with a valuation of $2 billion in 2021. Privately held. B2B software, no consumer awareness.

wiki.title: Unqork
wiki.text: Unqork is a cloud computing and enterprise software company based in New York, NY that offers a no-code development platform-as-a-service (PaaS) for building enterprise applications. Unqork supports organizations in finance, insurance, healthcare, and government.

about: Vectra AI is a US cybersecurity company, based in San Jose, California, founded in 2011, whose platform uses AI to detect and prioritise attacks across networks, cloud, identity and SaaS (the Attack Signal Intelligence approach). Customers are large enterprises and government agencies, with revenue from subscriptions. It raised about $353 million and was valued at $1.2 billion in 2021. Privately held. B2B brand with no consumer awareness.

wiki.title: Vectra AI
wiki.text: Vectra AI, Inc. is a cybersecurity company that uses AI for hybrid attack detection, investigation, and response (NDR) solutions. The company was established in 2011 and operates in 113 countries from its San Jose, California headquarters, with further locations in Singapore, Australia, and Japan.

about: Hyperscience is a US intelligent document processing company, based in New York, founded in 2014 by Peter Brodsky, whose machine learning platform extracts data from forms, emails and handwritten documents for banks, insurers and governments. Customers are large organisations paying subscriptions. It raised about $289 million, and was valued at over $1 billion in 2021. Privately held. B2B software brand, no consumer awareness.

SecurityScorecard is a US cybersecurity ratings company, based in New York and founded in 2013, whose platform scores organisations' security posture and third-party risk using outside-in data, plus supply chain risk tools and threat intelligence. Customers are enterprises, insurers and governments. It raised about $292 million, with a 2021 round. Privately held. B2B brand, known in security and risk circles, not by consumers.

Shift Technology is a French artificial intelligence software company, based in Paris and founded in 2014, providing AI-native decision automation, fraud detection and claims handling software to insurers worldwide. Customers are over 100 insurers in 25 countries, paying subscriptions. It raised about $320 million, with a $220 million Series D in 2021. Privately held. B2B insurtech brand with no consumer awareness.

Yugabyte is a US database software company, based in Sunnyvale, California, which develops the open-source YugabyteDB, a distributed SQL database for cloud-native applications, with a managed cloud service. Customers are enterprises including banks and retailers. It raised about $291 million, valued at $1.3 billion in 2021. Privately held. B2B developer brand, with no consumer awareness.

wiki.title: YugabyteDB
wiki.text: YugabyteDB is a high-performance transactional distributed SQL database for cloud-native applications, developed by Yugabyte.

about: Auvik Networks is a Canadian cloud-based network management software company, based in Waterloo, Ontario, whose platform automatically maps and monitors networks for managed service providers (MSPs) and IT teams. Founded in 2011, it has thousands of MSP customers worldwide and raised about $283 million, latest in 2021. Privately held. B2B IT software with no consumer awareness.

Mindtickle is a US sales readiness and enablement software company, based in San Francisco, founded in 2011, offering training, coaching, content and AI revenue tools to sales teams. Customers are large technology, finance and life sciences companies paying subscriptions. It raised about $281 million, including a 2021 round that valued it at $1.2 billion, and has a major India engineering centre in Pune. B2B software, no consumer awareness.

ScienceLogic is a US IT operations software company, based in Reston, Virginia, whose AI-driven monitoring and observability platform (SL1) automates IT discovery, monitoring and incident handling for large enterprises, service providers and government. Founded in 2003, it raised about $235 million. Customers are large organisations. Privately held. B2B brand with no consumer awareness.

wiki.title: ScienceLogic
wiki.text: ScienceLogic is a software and service vendor. It produces information technology (IT) management and monitoring software for IT Operations and cloud computing.

about: Beyond Identity is a US cybersecurity company, based in New York, founded in 2019 by Jim Clark and Tom Jermoluk, selling passwordless, phishing-resistant authentication and device trust based on cryptographic keys rather than passwords. Customers are enterprises and technology companies. It raised about $205 million, including a $100 million Series C in 2022. Privately held. B2B security brand, with no consumer awareness.

Front is a US customer communication software company, based in San Francisco, founded in 2013 by Mathilde Collin and Laurent Perrin, whose shared inbox and workflow tools let teams manage email, SMS, chat and social messages together, with AI assistance. Customers are thousands of companies paying subscriptions. It raised about $204 million and was valued at about $1.7 billion. B2B software with no consumer awareness.

Observe.AI is a US conversation intelligence and AI agent platform for contact centres, based in San Francisco (listed here as Redwood City), whose software transcribes and analyses calls, scores agents and automates customer service tasks. Customers are large enterprises and BPOs. It raised about $214 million, including a $125 million Series C in 2022. Privately held. B2B software with no consumer awareness.
cb_desc: Observe.Al builds Al Agents for Customer Service

about: Sentry is a US application monitoring company, based in San Francisco, founded in 2012, offering error and performance monitoring tools for developers, which started as an open-source project. Customers are over 100,000 organisations, from startups to large enterprises. It raised about $217 million, with a $90 million Series E in 2022 at a $3 billion valuation. B2B developer brand, well known to software engineers.

Tredence is a US data analytics and AI consulting company, based in San Jose, California, founded in 2013, with large delivery centres in India, serving retail, consumer goods, telecom, healthcare and industrial clients. It raised about $205 million, latest in December 2022. It has thousands of employees. B2B services brand, with no consumer awareness.

Immersive (formerly Immersive Labs) is a Bristol-based cyber security company whose platform measures and builds cyber readiness through hands-on exercises, simulations and crisis drills for security teams, developers and executives. Customers include large enterprises, financial firms and government bodies, paying subscription fees. Founded in 2017 and backed by investors including Insight Partners and Goldman Sachs, it has raised about $190 million, including a $75 million Series C in 2022. Privately held, with offices in the UK and US. B2B, little consumer brand awareness.

Virtana is a Palo Alto-based software company whose hybrid cloud optimisation platform gives enterprises observability, capacity planning and cost optimisation across on-premises infrastructure and public clouds, with AI-driven analytics. It was formerly known for infrastructure performance monitoring under the earlier Virtual Instruments name. Customers are large enterprises and service providers, paying software subscriptions. Crunchbase shows about $195 million raised. Privately held. B2B, with little brand awareness beyond enterprise IT.
cb_desc: Virtana is the hybrid cloud optimization platform for digi...

about: LinkSquares is a Boston software company that makes an AI-powered contract lifecycle management platform, helping legal and finance teams store, search, analyse and track contracts, with tools for reviewing and extracting key terms. It sells subscriptions to mid-sized and large companies. Founded in 2015, it has raised about $161 million, with a Series C in 2022. Privately held. Strictly B2B, with recognition in legal technology but no consumer awareness.
cb_desc: LinkSquares is an Al-powered contract lifecycle managemen...

about: Panzura is a data management company whose products give enterprises a global file system and hybrid cloud storage, enabling teams across multiple locations to access, protect and analyse unstructured data such as engineering and media files. Customers are large organisations in sectors like construction, engineering, media and government, paying software and subscription fees. Based in San Francisco, it has raised about $170 million. Privately held. B2B enterprise infrastructure, with little consumer awareness.
cb_desc: Panzura's data management solutions allow enterprises to...

wiki.title: Panzura
wiki.text: Panzura is a privately owned American software company based in San Francisco, California, that provides hybrid-cloud data management software and services for the enterprise software market. Its software helps users access, manage, analyze, and store unstructured data using techniques in distributed data consolidation, artificial intelligence, and network load balancing.

about: HackerOne is a San Francisco security company running a platform that connects organisations with a large community of ethical hackers for bug bounty programmes, vulnerability disclosure, penetration testing and continuous threat exposure management. Customers include technology firms, financial institutions and governments such as the US Department of Defense, paying platform and bounty fees. Founded in 2012, it has raised about $159 million. Privately held. Well known in the security industry, with little awareness among consumers.

wiki.title: HackerOne
wiki.text: HackerOne Inc. is a cybersecurity operations technology company managed by certified information system security professionals who conduct vulnerability threat assessments to identify bugs found on a website, application or server. It was one of the first companies to embrace and utilize crowd-sourced security and cybersecurity researchers as linchpins of its business model; pioneering bug bounty and coordinated vulnerability disclosure. As of December 2022, HackerOne's network had paid over $230 million in bounties. HackerOne's customers include U.S. Department of State, U.S. Department of Defense, General Motors, GitHub, Goldman Sachs, Chat

about: Sauce Labs is a San Francisco company offering cloud-based continuous testing for web and mobile applications, giving development teams access to thousands of real devices, browsers and operating systems to run automated and manual tests. Customers include large enterprises and software teams, who pay subscriptions. Founded in 2008, it has raised about $151 million, with backers such as Toba Capital and Riverwood. Privately held. B2B, well known to software testers and engineers, with no consumer awareness.
cb_desc: Sauce Labs provides cloud- based testing for mobile and....

wiki.title: Sauce Labs
wiki.text: Sauce Labs is an American cloud-based software testing company that provides a unified platform for quality assurance across the software development lifecycle (SDLC). It is headquartered in San Francisco, California.

about: Sift is a San Francisco company providing digital trust and safety software that uses machine learning, applied to a global network of data, to detect and prevent online fraud, including payment fraud, account takeover and abuse. Customers are online businesses such as marketplaces, fintechs and e-commerce brands, paying usage-based subscriptions. Founded in 2011, it has raised about $157 million, with investors including Insight Partners and Spark Capital. Privately held. B2B, recognised in fraud and risk circles with no consumer awareness.

wiki.title: Sieve
wiki.what: Tool for separation of solid materials by particle size
wiki.text: A sieve, fine mesh strainer, or sift is a tool used for separating wanted elements from unwanted material or for controlling the particle size distribution of a sample, using a screen such as a woven mesh or net or perforated sheet material. The word sift derives from sieve.

wiki.title: Sift (company)
wiki.text: Sift is an American software company that develops telemetry and observability infrastructure for hardware systems. The company was founded in 2022 by former SpaceX software engineers Austin Spiegel and Karthik Gollapudi. Its primary product is a platform used by engineering teams in the aerospace, defense, and autonomous systems industries to ingest, store, and analyze data from machine sensors. It is headquartered in Marina del Rey, California, and has raised approximately $67 million in venture capital.

about: Ceragon Networks is a wireless backhaul company, founded in Israel and listed on Nasdaq (CRNT), that makes microwave and millimetre-wave radio systems, 5G transport and private network solutions. Its US operations are based in Richardson, Texas, and Crunchbase lists the company there. Customers are mobile operators, utilities, governments and enterprises, buying equipment and services, and it has deployed networks in over 100 countries. B2B telecom equipment brand with little consumer recognition.

Happiest Minds Technologies is an Indian IT services and digital transformation company, founded in 2011 by Ashok Soota and based in Bengaluru, providing cloud, analytics, AI, cybersecurity, IoT and product engineering services to customers in banking, healthcare, retail, edtech and industrial sectors. It employs thousands of staff in India and offices in the US, UK and elsewhere. Revenue is from IT projects and managed services. Listed on the NSE and BSE since 2020. B2B, little consumer awareness.

Alt is a Tokyo-based Japanese artificial intelligence company, with an office in Roppongi, that develops large language models and AI products for businesses, such as the AI GIJIROKU meeting transcription service, and works on generative AI and cultural projects. Customers are Japanese companies and public bodies, and revenue is from software subscriptions and AI development. It listed on the Tokyo Stock Exchange in 2023. Crunchbase shows about 5.4 billion yen in funding. B2B, with some recognition in Japan's AI sector.

Fiverr is an Israeli-founded online freelance marketplace, with its registered and operational base in Tel Aviv and an office in New York, connecting buyers with freelancers offering services such as design, writing, programming and video, starting from low-priced gigs. Founded in 2010, it is listed on the NYSE (FVRR) and earns commissions and fees from both sides, plus Fiverr Pro and Fiverr Business offers. Millions of active buyers use it. Well-known consumer and small business brand with heavy advertising.

wiki.title: Fiverr
wiki.what: Israeli online marketplace for freelance services
wiki.text: Fiverr is an Israeli multinational online marketplace for freelance services. It connects freelancers to people or businesses looking for services. Fiverr takes its name from the $5 asking price attached to all tasks when the company was founded, though many sellers now charge more.

about: US managed cloud services company that helps enterprises run applications across AWS, Microsoft Azure, Google Cloud and private clouds, with consulting and managed security. Based in San Antonio, Texas; taken private by Apollo Global Management in 2016 and returned to Nasdaq (RXT) in 2020. Revenue about $2.7 billion, thousands of employees and a heavy debt load. Customers are mid-size and large organisations worldwide. Funding shown of about $543 million. Known in IT, not to consumers.

wiki.title: Rackspace Technology
wiki.text: Rackspace Technology, Inc. is an American information technology cloud computing company based in San Antonio, Texas. It also has offices in Reston, Virginia, as well as in Australia, Canada, United Kingdom, India, Dubai, Switzerland, the Netherlands, Germany, Singapore, Mexico, Toronto and Hong Kong. Its data centers are located in Amsterdam (Netherlands), Virginia (US), Chicago (US), Dallas (US), London (UK), Frankfurt (Germany), Hong Kong (China), Kansas City (US), New York City (US), San Jose (US), Shanghai (China), Queenstown (Singapore) and Sydney (Australia).

about: Sumo Logic is a Redwood City, California cloud-based log management, security analytics and observability platform used by DevOps and security teams to monitor applications and detect threats. Customers are software-driven enterprises paying subscriptions. Founded in 2010, it listed on Nasdaq (SUMO) in 2020 and was taken private by Francisco Partners in 2023 for about $1.7 billion. Crunchbase shows about $340 million raised before its IPO. B2B technology brand with little consumer awareness.

wiki.title: Sumo Logic
wiki.text: Sumo Logic, Inc. is a cloud-based data analytics company, focusing on cybersecurity, security analytics and observability. It provides log management and analytics services based on artificial intelligence.

about: Anaplan is a business planning software company, founded in San Francisco and shown with a Miami address in the input, that sells a cloud platform for connected planning across finance, sales, supply chain and workforce. Customers are large enterprises paying subscriptions. Founded in 2006, it listed on the NYSE (PLAN) in 2018 and was taken private by Thoma Bravo for about $10.7 billion in 2022. Crunchbase shows about $300 million raised in 2018. B2B software brand with little consumer awareness.

wiki.title: Anaplan
wiki.text: Anaplan is a business planning software company headquartered in Miami, Florida. Anaplan sells subscriptions for cloud-based business-planning software and provides data for decision-making purposes.

about: BrowserStack is a cloud-based software testing platform that lets developers test websites and mobile apps across thousands of real browsers and devices, with products for automated, visual and accessibility testing. Customers are software teams at companies of all sizes, paying subscriptions. Founded in 2011 in Mumbai, it has offices in Dublin (shown here), the US and India, and has raised about $250 million, with a valuation of $4 billion in 2021. B2B developer brand with little consumer awareness.

wiki.title: BrowserStack
wiki.text: BrowserStack is a cloud-based software testing platform founded in 2011. It provides tools for testing websites and mobile applications across multiple devices, browsers, and operating systems. The company is headquartered in Mumbai, with additional offices in San Francisco, New York, and Ireland.

about: Reltio is a Redwood Shores, California cloud-based data management company that provides a master data management and customer data platform to unify and clean company data using AI. Customers are large enterprises in life sciences, financial services and retail, paying subscriptions. Founded in 2011, it raised about $237 million, including a 2021 round. B2B data brand with little consumer awareness.

Sourcegraph is a San Francisco developer tools company that makes code search and code intelligence software, plus the Cody and Amp AI coding assistants that understand a company's whole codebase. Customers are software engineering teams at large enterprises and technology firms, paying subscriptions. Founded in 2013, it raised about $248 million from investors including Sequoia and Andreessen Horowitz. B2B developer brand with little consumer awareness.

wiki.title: Sourcegraph
wiki.text: Sourcegraph Inc. is a company developing code search and code intelligence tools that semantically index and analyze large codebases so that they can be searched across commercial, open-source, local, and cloud-based repositories.

about: Jumio is a Sunnyvale, California identity verification and anti-fraud company that uses AI to confirm that a person matches the government ID they present, via document and biometric checks, for onboarding and compliance. Customers are banks, fintechs, marketplaces, airlines and crypto firms, paying per verification. Founded in 2010, it raised about $205 million from investors including Great Hill Partners and Millennium Technology Value Partners. B2B brand with little consumer awareness.

wiki.title: Jumio
wiki.text: Jumio is an online mobile payment and identity verification company that offers card and ID scanning and validation products for mobile and web transactions. They sell these products under the brand name "Netverify Trusted Identity as a Service."

about: Airbyte is a San Francisco open-source data integration company whose platform moves data from hundreds of sources, such as databases and software-as-a-service apps, into data warehouses and lakes, with both a self-hosted and cloud version. Customers are data teams at start-ups and enterprises, paying for the cloud service and enterprise support. Founded in 2020, it raised about $181 million from investors including Benchmark and Coatue. B2B developer and data brand with little consumer awareness.

wiki.title: Airbyte
wiki.text: Airbyte is an open-source data integration platform that allows organizations to recompile and synchronize multi-source data in places such as data warehouses, data lakes or databases. Founded in 2020 with investments in San Francisco, California, the company offers multiple implementation offers, including cloud integration, local, and hybrid integration of data.

about: Mural is a San Francisco digital collaboration platform, with a virtual whiteboard for teams to brainstorm, plan and run workshops remotely, plus templates and facilitation tools. Customers are companies, design teams and consultants using it, paying subscriptions. Founded in 2011, it raised about $194 million from investors including General Catalyst and Insight Partners. B2B software brand with little consumer awareness.

wiki.title: Mural
wiki.what: Piece of artwork on a large permanent surface
wiki.text: A mural is any piece of graphic artwork that is painted or applied directly to a wall, ceiling or other permanent substrate. Mural techniques include fresco, mosaic, graffiti and marouflage.

about: GoodData.AI is a San Francisco analytics company that sells an AI-native decision intelligence and embedded analytics platform, letting software companies and enterprises add dashboards and metrics to their own products. Customers are software vendors and enterprises, paying subscriptions. Founded in 2007, it raised about $168 million. B2B analytics brand with little consumer awareness. It competes with embedded analytics and business intelligence vendors and sells to software companies and enterprises, so it has a technical brand with no consumer recognition.

wiki.title: GoodData.AI
wiki.text: GoodData.AI is a software company headquartered in San Francisco, California, in the U.S., with additional offices in Europe and Asia.
